set.title: Business continuity starter set
set.description: Four continuity procedures written by Resgrid as a starting point for agencies, dispatch centres and businesses: activating the continuity plan, losing communications, evacuating and relocating a facility, and running manually when the computer systems are down.

protocols.name: Continuity plan activation
protocols.description: Who can activate the continuity plan, and the first steps once it is active.

blocks.html: The continuity plan keeps essential functions running when people, facilities, systems or suppliers are lost.

items.html: The people named in your plan (and their alternates, in order) may activate it.
Notify leadership, staff and key partners that the plan is active, and say which functions come first.
Open a log of decisions, actions and costs from the moment of activation.
Review the situation at set intervals and decide when to return to normal operations.

protocols.name: Loss of communications
protocols.description: Fallback communication when phones, radio or data networks fail.

blocks.title: Fall back in this order (adapt to your systems)

items.html: Switch to the backup radio channel or talk group.
Use satellite phones or other independent links where you have them.
Send runners, and post staff at agreed meeting points.

blocks.title: Report the outage
blocks.html: Report the failure to the system owner and to neighbouring agencies who may be relying on you.

protocols.name: Facility evacuation and relocation
protocols.description: Leaving the primary facility and moving essential work to the alternate site.

items.html: Evacuate by the posted routes to the assembly point and account for everyone.
Take the go-kit if it is safe to do so.
Decide whether to relocate, and announce it to staff and partners.
Open the alternate site and restore essential functions in the plan's order.
Forward phone lines and update the addresses and numbers partners use to reach you.

protocols.name: Computer system outage: manual operations
protocols.description: Keeping dispatch and records work going on paper while computer systems are down, and catching up afterwards.

items.html: Announce the outage and switch to the paper forms and status boards in the downtime kit.
Number each incident by hand in the series your plan reserves, and note every time.
Track unit status on the board; confirm assignments by radio.
Enter the paper records into the system, oldest first, and keep the paper as the original.
Check unit statuses against the board before switching back.
